pages.title: Start Here
pages.html:
EasyNDF changes numbers in WARNO's and Steel Division 2's game files for you, like a weapon's range or how fast it reloads.

You describe each change once, as a rule. EasyNDF applies your rules to the files you add and gives you edited copies. The files you add are never changed, and nothing leaves your computer.

New Here?

  1. Four steps: the whole job, start to finish.
  2. Words used here: what a mod, rule set or descriptor is.

Never Made a WARNO Mod?

Making a WARNO mod covers the game's side: making a mod folder, building it and turning it on in the game.

TipEvery window in the app has a ? button. The search box on the left finds any page.

pages.title: Four Steps
pages.html:
1. Pick your rules. On the Mods tab, click a mod in the Mods list. WARNO Tactical Overhaul is a ready-made example. Import mod... loads a mod file someone shared.
  2. Add the files. On the Files tab, press Add folder... and choose a GameData folder, ideally the game's clean files.
  3. Try it. Press Preview. Nothing is saved. Click a file to see what changed in Details.
  4. Export. Press Run export and choose a folder; your edited files are written there. Choose your mod's folder to put them straight in your mod.
NoteClean files work best. Rules apply to whatever you add, so a file you already exported gets them again: "multiply by 2" becomes "multiply by 4". Run export asks before it does that to a file EasyNDF exported before.
TipNot sure what to press next? The green button is always the next step.

pages.html:

GameDataThe folder that holds the game's .ndf files.
ExportThe edited copies EasyNDF makes for you.
TipClick a word to read more about it.

pages.title: What Is an NDF File
pages.html:
An .ndf file is a text file that describes part of the game's data in WARNO and Steel Division 2: units, weapons, ammunition, divisions, the interface and the game's general settings.

NDF is a language for describing game data. A file defines objects, their properties, and how they relate to each other; the game reads the files when it starts and builds its data from them. So a number changed in a file is a change in the game.

The files are plain text. Any text editor opens them, and the Editor tab shows them in color.

Where They Are

Every mod has a GameData folder with the game's .ndf files in it, in subfolders by subject. WARNO\Mods\ModData (or Steel Division 2\Mods\ModData) is a complete mod with the game's current data, which Steam keeps up to date. Don't work in it: copy from it, so you always have clean files.

Some files worth knowing, all in GameData\Generated\Gameplay\Gfx:

  • UniteDescriptor.ndf: every unit.
  • WeaponDescriptor.ndf: each unit's turrets and the weapons on them.
  • Ammunition.ndf: what each weapon fires, such as its range and damage.

Making a WARNO mod covers making a mod of your own.

What Is Inside

A file is mostly a long list of descriptors (the manuals call them objects). Each one describes one thing: one unit, one weapon or one kind of ammunition. Here is a short one:

// Made-up example, simplified
export Ammo_Example_Cannon is TAmmunitionDescriptor
(
    DescriptorId    = GUID:{6f1c2a9e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001}
    Caliber         = "105mm"
    MaximumRangeGRU = 2450
    PhysicalDamages = 2.5
    IsGuided        = False
    Traits          = ['HE', 'AP']
    Weapon          = $/GFX/Weapon/Weapon_Example_Cannon
)

Reading a Descriptor

  • Ammo_Example_Cannon is its name. Other descriptors use the name to refer to it.
  • is TAmmunitionDescriptor is its type: what kind of thing it is. Types nearly always start with a T, and are defined inside the game, so a type's full list of properties can't be looked up. Descriptors of the same type have the same kinds of properties.
  • Everything between ( and ) belongs to the descriptor.
  • Each line inside, like MaximumRangeGRU = 2450, is a property: a name, an equals sign, and its value. Changing values is what a mod does. A property that is left out takes a default: usually 0, false, or empty.
  • // starts a comment, which the game ignores until the end of the line. Comments can also run over several lines between /* and */, or between { and }, which Steel Division 2 uses to switch off old lines.
  • Many descriptors start with export. Leave it as it is.

Kinds of Values

  • Number: whole, like 2450 or -1, or with a decimal point, like 2.5. Whole numbers can also be written in hexadecimal, like 0xFF00A8.
  • Text: in single or double quotes, like "105mm".
  • True or false: True or False (true and false work too).
  • List: values between square brackets, separated by commas, like ['HE', 'AP']. A list can hold any kind of value, including objects.
  • Pair: two values in brackets, like (22, 7).
  • Map: a list of pairs, each a key and its value, written MAP [ (1, 'one'), (2, 'two') ].
  • Object: a type followed by its own properties in brackets: a small descriptor inside a property. A unit's details, for example, sit in objects called modules.
  • Reference: the name of another descriptor, often in another file. It can be the name alone, a full path like $/GFX/Weapon/Weapon_Example_Cannon, or a path like ~/Weapon_Example_Cannon that starts from wherever the game loads the file. nil means it refers to nothing.
  • GUID: GUID:{...}, an ID for the descriptor. EasyNDF gives descriptors it adds or clones a new one, so each keeps its own.

A value can also be worked out, like 3 + 0.5 or 35 div 8 (NDF divides with the word div, also written DIV).

Effect, interface and template files also use conditions, like HasSound ? Sound : nil, comparisons like != and <, and parts of other objects, like Panel.Width[0]. EasyNDF reads them and keeps them exactly as written; rules change the plain values around them.

A line like Gravity is -9.81, with a value instead of a type and brackets, gives a name to a single value: a constant that other places can use.

How Files Connect

Descriptors refer to each other, often across files: a unit refers to its weapons, and a weapon to its ammunition. Change one descriptor and everything that refers to it gets the change. The descriptor list on the Editor tab follows these links.

Where EasyNDF Comes In

A rule picks descriptors by name, type or property, then changes their properties. Everything a rule doesn't change, including spacing and comments, stays exactly as it was (see What an exported file looks like).

TipTo see a real descriptor, open a file on the Editor tab and double-click a name in the list below the text.

pages.title: The Tutorial
pages.html:
The tutorial isn't in this version yet: Start the tutorial in the welcome window is greyed out. It will walk you through the app with a small sample file, needing no game files and saving nothing to your computer.

Until then, Four steps covers the whole job.

How It Will Work

  • Each step asks you to do one thing, shown in bold. When you do it, the tour moves on.
  • A step with a dashed outline is just for looking. Press Next.
  • While the tour runs, only the outlined part responds to clicks, so you can't get lost.
  • Back and Skip step, or the Left and Right arrow keys, move through it. The page changes to match the step you land on.
  • End tour stops it at any time. Escape does not.
TipThe sample file is removed when the tour ends. Changes you made yourself, like a watermark, are kept.

pages.title: Important to Know
pages.html:
NoteClean files work best. Rules apply to whatever you add, so a file you already exported gets them again: "multiply by 2" becomes "multiply by 4". Run export asks before it does that to a file EasyNDF exported before.
  • Your rules are saved on this computer only, in EasyNDF's data folder (see Backups and clearing data). Use Export mod on the Mods tab now and then to keep a copy.
  • Green, yellow, red: green means changed, yellow means changed but worth a look, red means it failed. Click the file to see why.

pages.title: The Files Tab
pages.html:
Add the game files you want to change, check which rules each one gets, then press Preview to try it and Run export to get the edited files.

Pages About This Tab

  • Adding files
  • The file list
  • Search, filter and folders
  • Preview and Run export

pages.title: Adding Files
pages.html:
• Add folder... adds every .ndf file in a folder and its subfolders. You can also drag a folder onto the window.
  • Add files... adds single files. A .zip or .rar, added or dropped on the window, is opened and the .ndf files inside it are added.
  • Only .ndf files are added. Anything else is skipped, and the app tells you.
  • Big folders (over 150 .ndf files) ask whether to add everything or only the files your mod has rules for.
  • Each file remembers which folder it came from. It's shown in small text under its name.
  • If you add a file that's already in the list, you're asked whether to replace it, keep both or skip it.
  • With Reopen the last files on in Settings, the list comes back as you left it when the app starts, with the files that are still where they were.

More About Adding

  • Dragging files over any tab switches to the Files tab.
  • The folder shown under a file starts with the folder you added.
  • Files a mod that is on has rules for are read straight away. The others say not read yet and are read when needed: when a rule set comes to apply to them, when you run them, or when you pick them under Property scan.
  • When you add a file that's already listed, the question shows how the two files differ. To stop being asked, choose an answer under Duplicate files in Settings.

pages.title: The File List
pages.html:
ColumnWhat it shows
OnWhether the file is included when you press Preview or Run export.
Source fileThe file's name, with its folder underneath.
ArmoryWhich parts of the Armory have changes for the file: Divisions, Battlegroups, Units, Weapons. A lit letter runs its rules on the file, after its mod's rule sets; its tooltip says how many. Click a letter to see that part on the Mods tab.
ModsThe mods that run on the file, in the order they run. Names that don't fit become 2 more; click to see them all, numbered, with the rule sets each runs. ⚠ marks a mod that changes a value another also changes.
StatusWhat happened last time. Green: done. Yellow: done, worth a look. Red: failed.
×Takes the file off the list. A file held back by the safety check also has Save anyway.
Size, Lines, Date modified, Export folderExtra details. Some are hidden at first; turn them on with Columns.

Working with the List

  • Click a row to select it. Ctrl-click adds or removes one. Shift-click selects a range.
  • Click the File list heading to collapse the list, and again to bring it back.
  • Remove takes files off the list. The files on your computer are never touched.
  • Click a column heading to sort by it. Click again to reverse.
  • Ctrl+Z undoes changes to the list.

More Columns

ColumnWhat it shows
#The row number, counted down the list as shown. Click it to sort by the order you added the files.
LinesBlank until the file has been read.

More About Selecting

  • Select all or Ctrl+A selects every row you can see. Press it again to select none.
  • Delete removes the selected rows, after asking. Remove all clears the list.
  • Export folder... sets where the selected rows are written.
  • Right-click a row to open it in the Editor, choose its export folder or remove it.

More About Sorting and Arranging

  • An arrow shows which column the list is sorted by.
  • Status sorts by what needs you first: errors, warnings, rules that changed nothing, no rules, ready, done, then files switched off.
  • Drag a column heading onto another to move it.
  • Reset columns, in the Columns list, puts back the original columns, order, sorting and widths.
  • Columns size themselves to fit. Drag the line between two headings to set a width yourself; double-click the line to go back to automatic.
  • Drag the bar between the list and Details to share the room differently. Double-click it to reset.
TipUndo brings a removed file back with its results.

pages.title: Search, Filter and Folders
pages.html:
• Search files shows only files whose name or folder contains what you type.
  • The box next to it shows one kind of file, like files with errors, or files with no rules.
  • Hidden files still run when you press Preview or Run export, as long as they're switched on.
  • Group by folder puts files under a line per folder. Its checkbox switches the whole folder on or off.

Filter Choices

  • Has rules or No rules
  • On or Off
  • Changed: the last run edited it.
  • Errors or warnings
  • A rule changed nothing
  • Not read: not read from your computer yet.

More About Folders

  • Click a folder line to open or close it.
  • Expand all and Collapse all open or close every folder.
  • While you search, folders with matching files open by themselves.

pages.title: Preview and Run Export
pages.html:
Preview

Runs your rules and shows what would change. Nothing is saved.

Run Export

  • Runs your rules and writes the edited files into each file's export folder.
  • Each Run export asks for the export folder, starting in the one used last. With Ask for the export folder each time off in Settings, a file with no export folder yet asks for one, and keeps it for next time.
  • Only files your rules changed are exported. Settings can change this.
  • Save as zip... packs the files the last export wrote into one .zip, keeping their folders.

Export Folders

Select files, press Export folder... and choose a folder; or right-click a row and choose Choose export folder.... EasyNDF won't write over the file it read from, so your originals are safe.

The Safety Check

Every edited file is checked before it's saved. If something would break the file, the row turns red and the file is held back. Save anyway lets you look at it.

While It Runs

  • Each row says where it is: Waiting, Working, then what happened, such as Exported to "MyMod": 12 edits.
  • A bar under the buttons shows the file being worked on and how far the run has got. Cancel stops after that file; files already exported stay as they are.
  • Each file is written whole or not at all, so a crash or a closed app never leaves half a file in your mod. Closing the app while an export runs asks first.

More About How Files Arrive

  • Each file is written in the same subfolders it had when you added its folder, so exporting into a mod folder puts everything in place.
  • Confirm before Run export, Back up overwritten files and Open the folder after export in Settings change how an export goes.
  • With Files to export set to every file, files your rules left alone, and files with no rules, are copied exactly as they were.

Warnings

  • A number that couldn't be read, a failed Check rule, or a rule that changed nothing turns the status yellow. Details explains it. The export still goes ahead.
  • A change that changes nothing, like multiplying 0 by 2 or setting a value to what it already is, isn't counted and gets no comment.
NoteRules run on whatever you add. Run on an earlier export, they apply twice: a value multiplied by 2 ends up multiplied by 4.

pages.title: What an Exported File Looks Like
pages.html:
• Only what your rules change is changed. Spacing, comments and everything else stay exactly as they were.
  • The first line says // Edited with EasyNDF and the version. You can turn this off in Settings.
  • An action can add a comment next to each changed value, with the old value, so you can see what changed right in the file.
  • Math results are rounded to 2 decimal places by default. Settings can change this.

More Details

  • Blank lines and one-line lists are copied as they were too. A file your rules didn't change comes out identical to the original.
  • An item added to a list is laid out like the list's other items.
  • An added or cloned descriptor is spaced the way the file spaces its own descriptors.
  • Text a rule adds is written exactly as you typed it in the rule. To match the file's column spacing, type it that way.
  • A removed descriptor or list item takes its same-line comment with it. Comments on the lines above it stay.
  • A watermark adds a second comment line at the top. Exporting a file again writes fresh lines; it never adds a second set.

More About Numbers

  • A result that would round to 0 without being 0 keeps its first digit, so 0.004 doesn't become 0.
  • Formula rules round with round() instead.
  • Whole numbers keep every digit, up to 15.

Line Endings

Follow the Line endings setting: LF, which the game uses, CRLF, or the same as each original file.

pages.title: Details
pages.html:
Click a file in the list to see what happened to it last time.

Details starts collapsed the first time the app opens: click its heading to open it. The app remembers whether you leave it open.

  • Each rule gets one line: how many descriptors it matched, how many values it changed, and how many it skipped.
  • Click a rule to see every value it changed, before and after.
  • Double-click a change to see it in the file, on the Editor tab.
  • Skipped means the rule found the value but couldn't change it, for example multiplying text.
  • A rule that changed nothing is pointed out. That's not an error, but after a game update it often means something was renamed.

The Mods Table

ColumnWhat it means
Descriptors matchedHow many descriptors met the rule's conditions.
EditsHow many values it changed.
SkippedHow many it found but couldn't change.

More Details

  • How many changes are listed per rule is set by Edits listed per rule in Settings. It doesn't limit the changes made.
  • Skipped also covers an item number past the end of a list.

Warnings

Listed above the rules:

  • A number that couldn't be read.
  • A Check rule that failed.
  • A descriptor renamed to a name another one already has.
  • A Table rule with two rows for the same descriptor. The last row is used.

pages.title: Mods and Rule Sets
pages.html:
• A mod holds rule sets. A rule set holds the rules for one file.
  • The app comes with My mod, empty, for your own rules, and WARNO Tactical Overhaul, a complete example.
  • Pick a mod in the Mods list on the Mods tab. + makes a new mod; right-click a mod to rename, copy, delete or export it. A mod file dropped on the list is imported. Drag the grips between the Mods, Rule Sets and rules columns to make them wider or narrower; double-click a grip to put its column back. Each mod's letters D B U W light up for the parts of the Armory it changes; click one to open them.
  • Mods run together. Every mod switched on runs on export and Preview, one after the other from the top of the list down, each on what the one above gave. Move a mod with Ctrl+↑ and Ctrl+↓, or right-click it. Each mod runs the rule sets that apply to the file, in the list's order. The Files tab's Mods column shows which mods run on each file.
  • When two mods that are on change the same value, the lower one wins, and both are marked ⚠ after the next Preview or export; hover over it for the values. A copy starts on or off as its original is, and an imported mod as it was when exported; a copy that is on beside its original changes everything twice. Undo takes back a switch or a move, and opens the mod whose change it takes back.
  • The Armory shows the values the mods that are on make, in their order. A mod that is off shows nothing there, and can't be changed there until it is switched on.
  • While the open mod is off, a line under the list says so, with Switch On; OK hides it until another mod is opened.
  • Export mod saves the whole mod as one file, to keep or to share. Import mod... loads one.
  • To move one rule set between mods, select it, press Ctrl+X, open the other mod and press Ctrl+V. Right-click offers the same.

Naming Rule Sets

A rule set applies to the files whose whole name its name holds, capitals included, like My mod (Ammunition.ndf) for Ammunition.ndf. The line under its rules' heading says which: "Applies to Ammunition.ndf". To choose other files, or several, click Change... there (or right-click the rule set, Applies To...), switch off From its name and tick the files. Two rule sets of one mod for the same file both run, in the list's order.

TipTwo files with the same name in different folders? Put the folder in the name: WTO (Strategic/GDConstants.ndf).

More About Mods

  • Both built-in mods can be renamed or deleted, and come back if you use Clear all data.
  • A copy is named "Name (Copy)", and further copies get a number.
  • You can also drop a mod file onto the page to import it.
  • If a mod with that name already exists, you're asked whether to replace it, keep both or skip.

More About Rule Sets

  • Click a rule set to open its rules. Ctrl-click or Shift-click selects several; Duplicate, Delete, Cut and Copy then act on all of them. Rename needs exactly one.
  • Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy and paste rule sets too.
  • Rule set text copied from the old EasyNDF desktop app can be pasted.
  • A name only has to be unique inside its mod. A pasted, duplicated or moved rule set whose name is taken gets a number.
CarefulIf saving ever stops working, a red notice appears at the top of the page. Export your mod to keep a copy elsewhere.

pages.title: Watermark
pages.html:
Watermark..., under the mod's right-click menu, adds a comment with your name, the mod's version and the game version to every file your mod exports.

  • It's off until you switch on Enable.
  • It's saved inside the mod, so anyone who exports your mod writes your credits too.
  • With Ask on export on, Run export asks if you want to update it first.

What It Looks Like

// Mod: WARNO Tactical Overhaul 1.4, by ShadowofChernobyl, for game version 189645

In the Window

  • Author, Mod version and Game version fill in the line. Only what you fill in is written.
  • When you're asked on export, Export saves what you changed, and Don't show me this again stops the question.

pages.title: Rules
pages.html:
• Rules run from top to bottom. The switch on the left turns a rule off.
  • The small symbol before a rule's name shows its type. Point at it to see the type's name; click it to open the rule.
  • To add one, press New rule and pick a type.
  • Double-click a rule to open it. Its window shows the name, the conditions and the actions.
  • Double-click a condition or action to change it in the window beside it. + adds a new one.
  • Any: one condition is enough. All: every condition must match.
  • Everything saves as you go. Ctrl+Z undoes.

Example: Make Cannons Shoot Twice as Far

  1. Make a rule set named after the file, like My mod (Ammunition.ndf).
  2. Press New rule and choose Edit rule.
  3. Add a condition: Descriptor Title, Starts With, Ammo_Canon.
  4. Add an action: target MaximumRangeGRU, Multiply, 2.
  5. Preview, and check the result in Details.

More About Adding Rules

  • A new rule goes in below the selected one and opens straight away.
  • In a mod with no rule set yet, a new or pasted rule first makes a rule set called "New rule set". Rename it after its file.
  • A switched-off rule's name is dimmed.

The Rule Window

  • Open a rule by double-clicking it, selecting it and pressing Enter, or right-clicking it and choosing Configure.
  • It shows the name and Enabled at the top, then Applies to, the conditions and the actions.
  • Done saves your changes. ×, Escape or a click outside closes it without saving, after asking.

More About Conditions and Actions

  • In the window beside the rule, ‹ and › step to the one above or below. Enter or Done keeps your changes; × or Escape takes them back. The rule window's Done saves them.
  • The + above a list adds a new one. The arrows move the selected ones.
  • While you type a property name, a value or a formula, a list suggests what fits: Enter or Tab puts it in, Escape closes it, and Ctrl+Space opens it. Point at a suggestion to see what it is.
  • Each has an optional Name, which shows in the list and goes into mod files.
  • In the Value box, Shift+Enter adds a line break.

Selecting and Keys

  • The ▾ on a Group heading folds or unfolds its rules; double-click the heading to open it. Expand all and Collapse all, in the right-click menu, or Ctrl+Shift+] and Ctrl+Shift+[, open or fold every group.
  • Click to select; Ctrl-click or Shift-click selects several. Rules hidden in a folded group are left out of Shift-click and Ctrl+A.
  • Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+↑, Ctrl+↓, Ctrl+A and Delete act on the list you clicked last. It has a green border.
  • In a list of conditions or actions, Up and Down move the selection; with Shift they extend it.
  • Right-click a rule, condition or action for a menu: Configure, Duplicate, Move, Cut, Copy, Disable or Enable, Delete, Create New and Paste.

Copy and Paste

Copied items go through the clipboard as text, so they can move between rules, rule sets and mods, and to and from the old desktop app. What you paste goes where it belongs: a rule set into the open mod, a rule into the open rule set, a condition or action into the open rule. It goes in below the selected row.

More About Undo

  • Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y, or Undo and Redo in the right-click menus, undo and redo any change to mods, rule sets, rules, conditions and actions, including importing a mod, and to the file list.
  • Typing in one box counts as one step. Inside a text box, Ctrl+Z undoes your typing there.
  • The history is forgotten when you close the app. Undo steps in Settings sets how far back it goes.
CarefulDeleting a Group heading asks first, because the rules under it then belong to a different group, or to none. Moving a heading moves its rules with it.
TipA rule of a type this version doesn't know, from a newer mod file, is kept but switched off and labelled.

pages.title: Rule Types
pages.html:
TypeWhat it does
✎Edit ruleChanges values in every descriptor that matches. The one you'll use most.
⊞Add descriptorAdds a new descriptor, written exactly as you type it.
⧉Clone descriptorCopies a descriptor under a new name, then changes the copy.
⊟Remove descriptorsDeletes every descriptor that matches. Needs at least one condition.
⇄Find and replaceReplaces a value wherever it appears.
⇅ScaleChanges a number, then rounds it and keeps it within limits you set.
ƒFormulaWorks out a value from other values, like round(0.8 * MaximumRangeGRU, 25).
▦TableApplies values pasted from a spreadsheet: one row per descriptor.
⌕LookupChanges descriptors based on a list in another file.
¶TextsAdds texts to a dictionary file such as UNITS.csv: one line per token.
❏FilePuts a file of your own into the mod on export: a picture, a video, a new NDF file.
✓CheckChanges nothing. Warns you when the number of matches isn't what you expect, which catches renames after a game update.
🗀GroupA heading with one on/off switch for the rules under it.
𝑥VariableA named value you can use in other rules as {Name}. Change it once to change many rules.
CarefulEvery type except Edit rule changes everything when it has no conditions.

More About Each Type

TypeGood to know
Edit ruleWith "Any" and no conditions, it matches nothing.
Add descriptorGoes at the end of the file, or after a descriptor you name. Skipped if the name already exists or the text isn't valid. The text box works like the File Editor.
Clone descriptorThe copy gets its own GUIDs, the same ones on every export. Later rules can change it too.
Remove descriptorsComments above a removed descriptor are kept.
Find and replace"Whole value only" leaves longer values that merely contain the text alone.
ScaleA step of 1 keeps whole numbers whole.
FormulaSkips a descriptor that lacks a value it needs.
TableOne column per property. Empty cells are left alone; unknown names are listed under Skipped.
LookupThe other file must be on the Files tab. It's read as it was loaded, before its own rules.
CheckA failed check doesn't stop the export.
GroupCovers every rule down to the next group, and can have shared conditions. Its ▾ folds it; double-click its heading to open it.
VariableApplies to the whole rule set, wherever it sits in the list, unless its group is switched off.
TextsOne TOKEN;Text per line. Its rule set must apply to a dictionary file on the Files tab (a .csv such as UNITS.csv or INTERFACE_OUTGAME.csv), which is exported with the lines added, in place of lines with the same token. When two mods give the same token, the lower one wins. A dictionary file goes into the mod's Localisation folder.
FileChoose the file and type where it goes in the mod, such as GameData/Assets/2D/Interface/Logo.png. It is written on export, into the folder that holds the GameData (or CommonData) folder of a file its rule set applies to. EasyNDF keeps its own copy, and Export mod carries it with the mod. Switch the rule off and the next export takes the file out again, unless it was changed since.
TipRule sets that use anything but plain Edit rules won't work in the old EasyNDF desktop app.

pages.title: What a Rule Applies To
pages.html:
A rule normally looks at each descriptor in a file. Some files are built differently, so some rules have an Applies to choice:

  • Each object of one type: for things inside other things, like one terrain in Terrains.ndf.
  • Top-level constants: for lines like Helico_MaxStunDamages is 450.

Which Rules Have It

Edit, Find and replace, Scale, Formula and Check rules.

Each Object of One Type, in Detail

  • Give the type, for example TGameplayTerrain, then a condition such as Name Is Equal To ForetDense.
  • Conditions and targets only see that object.
  • Descriptor Title is the title of the descriptor the object sits in, so a title condition still picks the unit.
  • A Group above the rule still tests the whole descriptor.

Top-level Constants, in Detail

As in DamageModules.ndf. All of them together count as one descriptor, and each is a property of it, so the target is the constant's name.

TipDetails names such an object by its descriptor, its type and its Name, when it has one.

pages.title: Conditions
pages.html:
Conditions pick which descriptors a rule changes.

The Three Boxes

BoxWhat goes in itExample
OperandWhat to look at: the descriptor's name, its type, all its text, or a property.Descriptor Title
OperatorThe test.Starts With
ValueWhat to test against.Ammo_Canon

Tests You Can Use

  • Text: Starts With, Ends With, Contains, Does Not Contain, Is Equal To, Is Not Equal To.
  • Numbers: Is Less Than, Is Greater Than, and their "Or Equal To" versions.
  • Lists: Contains Any Of, Contains All Of. Separate values with commas.
Careful"Does Not Contain" and "Is Not Equal To" are also true when the descriptor doesn't have that property at all.

More Than One Condition

Any means one condition is enough. All means every condition must match. Pick it next to the Conditions heading in the rule window.

Shortcuts

  • Enter or double-click opens the selected condition.
  • Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy it to another rule.
  • Ctrl+↑ and Ctrl+↓ move it.

Testing One Item of a List

Tick Custom and write the list's name with the item in square brackets: Salves[0] (counting from 0), Salves[FirstIndex], Salves[LastIndex] or Salves[LastIndex-1].

Good to Know

  • A property is found at any depth inside the descriptor.
  • Quoted values match with or without their quotes.
  • Conditions read values in one fixed layout, whatever the file's spacing, and never see comments.
  • Hover over an operand to read its full name.

pages.title: Actions
pages.html:
Actions make the changes.

  • Target is the property to change.
  • Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide change a number. Set To replaces the value.
  • Append, Prepend, Remove change text.
  • Set To [list, object] replaces a whole list or object with the value typed.
  • Add Property adds a property the descriptor does not have yet; Remove Property takes one out, its line and all. The comments above it stay.
  • On a list, Insert and Replace take index:value, counting from 0.
  • Comment writes a note next to each changed value in the file.
CarefulWrite numbers plainly, like 1.5. 1,5 or 2x won't work.

More About Targets

  • A target is found at any depth inside the descriptor.
  • It can also be the key of a pair, like a MAP entry: EVisionRange/Standard.
  • To change it only inside one property, write the path: MatrixCostName_X > EFactory/Tanks.
  • A path that starts with > starts at the descriptor's own properties and goes down one level per part: > ComponentFrame > Size leaves the ComponentFrame of anything inside it alone.
  • Not in the list? Tick Custom and type it.

More About Operators

  • A value written with a decimal point keeps one after Add, Subtract, Multiply or Divide.
  • Append, Prepend and Remove work inside the quotes of a quoted value. They also work on Descriptor Title and Descriptor Type.
  • Insert and Replace take an index that is a number, FirstIndex, LastIndex, or something like LastIndex-1.
  • Insert also takes Before X or After X: beside the first item whose text holds X, such as Before "Unite": "MyTag". When no item holds X, it goes at the end.
  • A list set with Set To [list, object] can be added to by later actions and rules.
  • Remove on a list takes the item to remove. To take out an object in a list by its type, such as a unit's module, use a Remove descriptors rule with Applies to set to that type.
  • A list or object typed on several lines takes the indentation of the line it goes on.

More About Comments

  • Left empty, the comment says what the action did, such as "Multiplied by 2". Text you type is used instead.
  • Edited by adds the mod's name, with its watermark version if it has one. Off by default.
  • Original value adds the old value; Timestamp adds the date.
  • A // note is moved to the end of its line, so it can't hide what follows.
TipType \n in a value for a line break. A number written wrongly is refused with a warning, and the value is left alone.

pages.title: Variables and Formulas
pages.html:
• A Variable rule gives a value a name, like RangeMultiplier = 2. Write {RangeMultiplier} anywhere else to use it.
  • A Formula works out a value. It can use numbers, property names, + - * /, brackets, and value for the current value.
  • Formulas also know min, max, abs, floor, ceil and round.

More About Variables

A variable can be used in any value, condition, table cell or formula.

More About Formulas

Put a name with a slash in square brackets: [EVisionRange/Standard].

Functions

FunctionWhat it does
min(a, b), max(a, b)The smaller or larger of two values.
abs(x)The value without its minus sign.
floor(x), ceil(x)Round down or up to a whole number.
round(x)Round to the nearest whole number.
round(x, step)Round to the nearest step, like 25.

pages.title: Property Scan
pages.html:
The lists of properties in the rule window come from a game file. EasyNDF reads, or "scans", that file to fill them.

  • The file matching your rule set's name is picked for you, if it's on the Files tab.
  • Pick another file under Property scan at the bottom of the rule window, or press ... to scan a file that isn't on the list.
  • "(not in scan)" next to a name just means the scanned file doesn't have it.
  • Need a name that isn't in the list? Tick Custom and type it.

More Details

  • A file you pick yourself is remembered for that rule set.
  • A file marked "not read yet" is read when you pick it.
  • When two files share a name, the open list shows each one's folder beside it.
  • Right-click the Property scan box to forget a scan.

pages.title: The Editor Tab
pages.html:
Read or edit any .ndf file, and see exactly what your rules change in it.

Pages About This Tab

  • Opening a file
  • Finding and editing
  • Seeing your changes
  • Descriptors

pages.title: Opening a File
pages.html:
The Editor tab shows any .ndf file with colors, so it's easier to read.

  • Double-click a file on the Files tab to open it.
  • Or pick one in the box at the top of the Editor, or press Open file....
  • Every file opens ready to edit, however long it is.
  • The file on your computer is never changed. Save as... saves your edited copy.
  • Click the File editor or Descriptor Tree heading to collapse that part, and again to bring it back.

More Details

  • You can also right-click a file on the Files tab and pick Open in editor.
  • Only the lines on screen are drawn, so even very long files stay quick to type in and scroll.
  • The Tab key types four spaces.
  • The colors come from your theme.
  • Discard changes goes back to the file as it was opened.

pages.title: Finding and Editing
pages.html:
• Find searches the file. Enter goes to the next match.
  • Replace and Replace all change what you found.
  • Go to line jumps to a line number.
  • Search all files searches every file on the Files tab at once.
  • Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo.
  • Ctrl+Scroll makes the text bigger or smaller. The strip under the text shows the line and column, and the size: pick one from its list.
  • The small arrows next to line numbers fold a block away. The buttons above the text fold or unfold everything.

More About Problems

  • Half a second after you stop typing, text that cannot be read gets a red wavy line. Point at it to see what is wrong.
  • The strip under the text shows the problem, or how many there are. Click it to go there, or to list them all; a click on one in the list goes to it.

More About Find and Replace

  • Find ignores upper and lower case. The down arrow or Enter goes to the next match; the up arrow or Shift+Enter to the previous one.
  • Replace changes the selected match and finds the next. Both Replace buttons need the text to be editable, and Ctrl+Z undoes them.

More About Searching All Files

  • Results list each matching line with its file and line number. Click one to open that file there.
  • Drag the bottom right corner of the results to resize them; × closes them.

More About Folding

Find, Go to line, Save as... and the export always use the whole text, folded or not.

CarefulDeleting a folded line deletes its whole block. Backspace right after a folded block, or Delete just before it, unfolds it instead. Folding never changes the text or the undo history.
TipWhile typing, Ctrl++, Ctrl+− and Ctrl+0 change the text size too. The size is remembered.

pages.title: Seeing Your Changes
pages.html:
• Show export shows the file as your rules would change it. Show source goes back.
  • Changes only shows just the changed lines, once the file has been run with Preview or Run export on the Files tab. A minus marks the old line, a plus the new one.
  • Use in file list sends your hand-edited text to the Files tab, so your rules apply to it.

More Details

  • Show export is read-only. Both views open at the same place in the file, so they're easy to compare.
  • It shows the last export if the page still has it; otherwise it runs your rules there and then.
  • Changes only shows two lines around each change, numbered as in the original and the export. Press it again to see the whole file.
  • Edits you typed in the Editor show too, and the note above counts rule edits and typed edits separately.
TipIn Details, double-click a change to jump to it here.

pages.title: Descriptors
pages.html:
Under the text is a list of the file's descriptors, with their properties on the right.

  • Open a descriptor to see what's inside it and what it links to, like a unit, its weapons and their ammunition.
  • Used by shows everything that refers to it. Changing it changes it for all of them.
  • Double-click a descriptor to find it in the text.
  • The box above the list finds any descriptor by name.
  • The funnel button beside it filters by property, such as every descriptor with a MaximumRangeGRU over 2000. The number on it is how many conditions are on.

The Filter

  • Each condition is a property, a test and a value. all or any above the list says how many must match.
  • The Property list holds the properties found in the descriptors being viewed: this file, or every read file under All files. (Name) and (Type) are always there.
  • A condition can have a Name, shown in the list in place of its details.
  • The checkbox turns a condition on or off. Right-click a condition to disable, duplicate, move, cut, copy, paste or delete it; the same keys as the Mods tab work.
  • Quotes around values are ignored, and text is compared without regard to capitals. "is greater than" and "is less than" compare numbers.
  • A filter works without saving it, and stays on until you clear it. Save as... keeps it under a name; Export and Import... share saved filters as a file.

More Details

  • A descriptor from another file is found once that file has been read. Refresh reads every file on the Files tab.
  • This file lists this file's descriptors. All files shows chains that lead from one file into another, like a unit leading to its weapon.
  • Alt+click a descriptor to find it in the text, too. This opens its file if it's in another one.

Changing a Value

  • When the descriptor is in the open file and the text is editable, type over a value and press Enter.
  • A value that would break the descriptor is refused.
  • Values that run over several lines are changed in the text itself.
TipDrag the bar between the two lists to share the width differently.

pages.title: The Armory Tab
pages.html:
See every unit of WARNO or Steel Division 2, or of a mod, with its stats, weapons and picture, read straight from the game.

Pages About This Tab

  • Where the units come from
  • Finding units
  • Comparing units
  • Changing divisions
  • Making units
  • Changing units
  • Changing a unit's weapons
  • Weapons
TipRight-click a unit or a weapon to open its descriptor in the File Editor, or to make a rule for it.

pages.title: Where the Units Come From
pages.html:
The Source box lists the games found in your Steam libraries (wherever Steam is installed), then the mods in each game's Mods folder.

  • Nothing is read until you choose a source, each time the app starts: reading a game's units and pictures takes a few seconds.
  • A game's units are read from its own files: Mods\ModData\base.zip for the NDF files, and the game's data for pictures, flags and names.
  • A mod's units are its own NDF files, with anything it does not change taken from the game. Its own unit pictures are used where it has them.
  • Mods added to the Mods folder show up the next time the list is opened.
  • The values shown are the ones the mods that are on make: their rule sets are run on the unit files on the Files tab, top to bottom. A value a rule changes has a * after it, in the heading colour; its tooltip names the mod, the rules and the game's value. Files not on the Files tab are shown as the game has them.
  • Show mods' changes, under the Source, switched off, shows the source as it is, with no mod's changes; values can't be changed then. The line beside it names the mods that are on, in the order they run; click it for the whole list.
  • Game not found? Choose Choose a Game Folder... and pick the game's folder: the one with Data and Mods in it.
  • The first time a picture is shown, it is taken from the game's files and kept, so it shows at once after that. Clear all data on the Settings tab deletes the kept pictures.
NoteThe Armory tab only reads the game. Nothing in the game's folder is changed.

pages.title: Finding Units
pages.html:
The filters on the left, and the tabs above the list, narrow down the units shown.

  • Find matches a unit's name or its descriptor's name.
  • Both and the side buttons, the role and the division lists, and Only units in a division narrow it further. That switch is on at first, as units in no multiplayer division are mostly for the campaign.
  • Only modded units shows only the units vanilla WARNO doesn't have: those your mod adds, and those of the game mod chosen as the source. The Add Units window has the same choice: All units, Vanilla units or Modded units.
  • Tick nations to show only them; All clears the ticks. The numbers are how many units each would show.
  • The tabs above the list (ALL, INF, TNK...) choose a factory.
  • Cards groups the units by role; click a role's heading to fold it. Table lists one unit a row; click a heading to sort by it.
  • Click a unit to see it in the Unit pane. Double-click it to open it in the File Editor.

From a Unit to Its Files

  • Right-click a unit or a weapon for Show ... in File Editor: the unit, its weapon set, the weapon's ammunition or missile. The file must be on the Files tab; if it isn't, the item is greyed.
  • New Rule for This Unit... makes an Edit rule in the open rule set, already matching the unit. New Rule for the Units Shown... matches every unit the filters leave.

pages.title: Comparing Units
pages.html:
Compare puts units side by side, each on a card across the width, with as many units as you like.

  • Add units with Compare on a unit, or + Add Units..., which finds units by name, side, type, nation and role. Tick several, then Add.
  • The first unit is pinned: every other card shows how far each stat is from it, and a line on each bar marks where the pinned unit's reaches. Pin another from its ▾ or by right-clicking it.
  • The best value of each stat among the units compared is in green and bold; for cost, the lowest is best.
  • Ranges are in the game's own units in WARNO (GRU), and in metres in Steel Division 2.
  • In a narrow window the weapons are left out, so the cards always fit.

pages.title: Changing Divisions
pages.html:
Choose a division in the list on the left to see its units by type, and change it in the Division pane and on its cards.

  • Its details (name, nation, type, activation points, place in the list), its emblem, its signature units and its card slot costs are in the Division pane and its cards' headings.
  • Click a card's veterancy marks to change its cards, units per card, veterancy and transports.
  • + in the division list's heading makes a new division: 50 activation points, the game's usual card slot costs, no emblem, last in the list.

Generated Divisions

  • ⚙ in the division list's heading opens Generate Divisions: one division for each nation and side you tick, times each kind you tick. Unlimited gives every unit 999 a card; Same for every unit gives each the numbers you type, one for each veterancy (10 · 6 · 3 · 1 at first); As the game's divisions gives each unit the numbers of the game division most generous with it; a unit no division has gets those of the units most like it (the same category, then the same type, the closest in cost). Game divisions or rules you name can be left out of what is learnt from, such as single-player challenges.
  • Units are listed A to Z. Nations the mods add of their own (no unit of the game is of them) can go into every division, of either side.
  • Every unit gets every transport the game accepts for it among the division's own units (those that fly first, then the dearest), and the division has the card slots you choose in each category, each costing 1 point.
  • A generated division keeps how it is made, not its units: they are made again from the files on the Files tab each time you export, so it follows game updates. It also needs UniteDescriptor.ndf on the Files tab. When nothing changed since the last export, the units made then are used again.
  • It shows ⚙ in the list, and a line above its units says how it is made, with Change… and Make Fixed. Make Fixed keeps the units it has now, as an ordinary division you change unit by unit.
  • Its generated numbers are dimmed. A value you change is kept on top, with a *, and stays when the division is made again.
  • Each one adds to the exported DivisionRules.ndf (about 1.5 MB for a big nation's, some 9 MB for every unit of both sides): the window says how much before you generate.

Generated Battlegroups

  • A generated division's Official Battlegroup is generated too: its cards are chosen from the division's units at each export, so they follow game updates. It needs Decks.ndf, DeckPacks.ndf, WeaponDescriptor.ndf, Ammunition.ndf and AmmunitionMissiles.ndf on the Files tab.
  • ⚙ Generation Settings… in the Battlegroups heading opens its settings. Start From gives ready weights: Balanced, Strongest, Cheapest, Anti-tank and Air defence; moving a slider makes them Custom.
  • What Matters Most weighs eight measures of each unit, from 0 to 100: against armour, against infantry, against aircraft, survivability, mobility, recon and optics, value for points and variety. Each unit is marked against the best of its category on each, and its score is the weighted mean.
  • For Each Role takes, among each role's units, the best, the one with good value (the most score for its cost) and the cheap one (the cheapest with at least half the best one's score). Variety spreads the cards across roles.
  • Size: the cards each type gets at most (never more than the division has room for), and the activation points at most (empty: the division's own).
  • Each change redraws the battlegroup behind the window, its new cards outlined, and What Changes lists the cards added and dropped. Done keeps the settings; Cancel changes nothing.
  • A generated card's tooltip says why it was chosen. Its cards can't be changed by hand: Make Fixed keeps the cards as they are, as an ordinary battlegroup you change card by card.

Saved as Rules

  • Every change is saved in the open mod as a rule in its Divisions rule set, under Armory Changes on the Mods tab (battlegroup changes in its Battlegroups rule set), one rule per change, under a group for each division.
  • These rules are locked (🔒): change them in the Armory, or open one and choose Make Editable to keep it by hand from then on.
  • A value the open mod changes has a * after it, in the heading colour; its tooltip says which rule changed it, and the game's value.

Files It Needs

  • The changes are written into Divisions.ndf, DivisionRules.ndf, DivisionCostMatrix.ndf and DeckSerializer.ndf, DivisionTextures.ndf for an emblem picture of your own, and the mod's own UNITS.csv (in its GameData/Localisation folder) for a name or a new division: the game looks division names up in it.
  • Add them to the Files tab first: a change that needs a file that is not there is refused, and the message says which to add.
  • On export, the Divisions rule set runs on these files after their own rule set. A new UNITS.csv is exported with the names, and your pictures are copied beside the exported Divisions.ndf, in the export folder's GameData folder.

pages.title: Making Units
pages.html:
On the Units sub-tab, + New Unit... makes a unit of your own in the open mod, in four steps listed at the top of its window.

  1. Model: choose the unit yours is a copy of: its 3D model, animations, showroom view, card picture, type, weapons and values all come with it. The panel at the right says what is copied.
  2. Name and Nation: its name, nation and role, and its card picture: Same as the unit it copies, or My own.... Its card at the left shows how it will look.
  3. Stats: its cost, strength, speed, optics and the other values, and its armor. A box left empty keeps the copied unit's value, shown dim in it; only the values you type are changed.
  4. Weapons: the copied unit's weapons turret by turret, as the Unit pane's Loadout section shows them, to swap, change, take off or add (see Changing a Unit's Weapons). Left as they are, your unit keeps them all.

Right-click a unit for Duplicate Unit... to copy it whole under a new name, with nothing else to choose, or use Duplicate... in the Unit pane. A unit you made has Delete Unit on its menu; it is taken out of your divisions too. Put your unit in a division from its menu, as any other.

Saved as Rules

  • Each unit is saved in the open mod as rules in its Units rule set, under Armory Changes on the Mods tab, under a group with the unit's name: a Clone rule that copies the unit and gives the copy its name and the values you changed, a rule giving it a deck code number, and for a card picture of your own, a rule adding it to the game's unit pictures.
  • Its values have a * after them, in the heading colour: they are all your mod's.
  • Nothing of the copy is taken away, such as its weapons: a unit missing something its 3D model expects can stop the game from loading, with no error. Change weapons with rules of your own, for now.

Files It Needs

  • A unit is written into UniteDescriptor.ndf and DeckSerializer.ndf, ButtonTexturesUnites.ndf for a card picture of your own, and the mod's own UNITS.csv for its name. Add them to the Files tab first: a unit that needs a file that is not there is refused, and the message says which to add.
  • On export, your card picture is copied into the export folder's GameData folder, where the game looks for it.

pages.title: Changing Units
pages.html:
On the Armory tab, change any unit of WARNO in the Unit pane: the game's own units and the ones you made.

  • The pane is in sections that fold, as the Division pane's: Unit (name, nation, role), Stats, Armor, Weapons, Specialties, Divisions and Files.
  • Under the buttons, Linked To says what else a change can reach: the divisions the unit is in, the units sharing its loadout (which always carry the same weapons), and its weapons other units carry too.
  • Click a value to change it: Enter keeps it, as does clicking elsewhere, and Esc puts it back. The nation and role are chosen from lists.
  • A box outlined in the caution colour holds a value the game does not take, and is put back. An armor level must be one the unit's armor family has, as the game's DamageResistance.ndf gives it: its tooltip says which.
  • The ✎ on the picture gives the unit a card picture of your own, or its own picture back.
  • The Loadout section changes its weapons: see Changing a Unit's Weapons.

Saved as Rules

  • A change to one of the game's units is saved in the open mod as an Edit rule in its Units rule set, under Armory Changes on the Mods tab, under a group with the unit's name. It sets only the values you changed; nothing of the unit is taken away.
  • A changed value has a * after it, in the heading colour; its tooltip says which rule changed it, and the game's value.
  • To see changed values like any other, turn off Mark changed values on the Settings tab, under Armory; their tooltips still say what changed them.
  • Type the game's value back, use Undo, or delete the rule on the Mods tab, to have the game's unit again.

Files It Needs

  • UniteDescriptor.ndf, ButtonTexturesUnites.ndf for a card picture of your own, and the mod's own UNITS.csv for a new name. Add them to the Files tab first: a change that needs a file that is not there is refused, and the message says which to add.

pages.title: Changing a Unit's Weapons
pages.html:
The Unit pane's Weapons section, and the New Unit window's Weapons step, show a unit's weapons as the game lays them out: turret by turret, each weapon with its ammo box.

  • A turret is a part of the unit's 3D model that turns and carries weapons. Weapons on one turret may share an ammo box, whose salvos they all fire from.
  • Type a box's salvos in Box 1 · 40 salvos, on the first weapon firing from it, and how many of a weapon are mounted in Count · ×1. Enter keeps the number; a changed one has a *.
  • Swap ▾ puts another weapon in a place, or the game's weapon back. The place keeps its turret, its ammo box, and its flash and sound, so a weapon of another kind fires with the old one's. The Swap window sorts the weapons by whether they fit: Fits this slot, Other kinds, and May not work here, each saying why: a missile needs a missile launcher, a weapon that must deploy to fire needs a place where one does, and weapons sharing an ammo box must fire the same number of shots a salvo. Nothing is refused: using one that may not work asks first, with I Know What I'm Doing.
  • Use a Copy to Change... in the Swap window, or Copy and Change... on a weapon, mounts a copy of your own, which you change on the Weapons sub-tab without changing the other units that carry the original.
  • ✕ takes a weapon off, and + Add to this turret... mounts another, with an ammo box of its own. Neither has been tried in the game yet: a 3D model may expect its weapons, and the game can fail to load with no message. Try them on a test mod first.
  • A changed weapon has a bar at its left and shows the one it replaced; one taken off stays in the list, faded and struck through, with Undo; one added has its own ✕.
  • Checks, beside the turrets in the New Unit window and under them in the Unit pane, say what the changes do, what hasn't been tried in the game, which files they need, and how they are written.

Double-click a weapon, or choose Show in Weapons from its right-click menu, to see it on the Weapons sub-tab. The menu also shows it in the File Editor, or makes a rule for it.

Saved as Rules

  • A unit with changed weapons gets a loadout of its own: a copy of the one it had in WeaponDescriptor.ndf, named WeaponDescriptor_EZ_..., and the unit is pointed at it. Only that copy is changed, so no other unit's weapons change.
  • The rules are in the open mod's Units rule set, with the unit's other changes. They need WeaponDescriptor.ndf and the unit's file on the Files tab.
  • Take a change back with its button in the list, with Undo, or by deleting the unit's rules from the Units rule set.

pages.title: Weapons
pages.html:
The Armory's Weapons sub-tab shows every weapon of the source, as cards or in a table, with the one you click in the Weapon pane.

  • A weapon here is one of the game's ammunition descriptors (Ammunition.ndf, and AmmunitionMissiles.ndf for missiles): its range, damage, accuracy, reload and picture.
  • Weapons are shared: every unit that carries one uses the same descriptor. Each card says how many units carry it, and the pane's Used By section lists them; click one to see it on the Units sub-tab.
  • A unit's loadout (which weapons it carries, on which turret, how many) is the unit's own, in WeaponDescriptor.ndf.

Finding Weapons

  • Type in Find to look for a name or descriptor. The tabs above the weapons choose a category: guns, autocannons, machine guns, small arms, anti-tank missiles, rockets, anti-air, artillery, aircraft weapons and smoke. The table shows the weapons under a heading for each.
  • The side and the nations are those of the units that carry a weapon: tick nations to see only the weapons their units carry.
  • In the table, click a heading to sort by it, and again for the other way.
  • Cards and Table each keep their own zoom: Ctrl and the mouse wheel over the weapons, Ctrl+plus, Ctrl+minus (Ctrl+0 for 100%), or the list at the bottom right.

Comparing Weapons

  • Right-click a weapon and choose Compare, or click Compare in the Weapon pane. Compare at the top shows them side by side.
  • The first weapon added is pinned: the others show how far each value is from its own, better or worse, and a bar with a mark where the pinned weapon's reaches. The best value of the weapons compared is in the "good" colour.
  • Right-click a card, or click ▾, to pin another weapon or take one off Compare.

The values shown are the open mod's, as its rules make them. A value your mod changes has a * after it; its tooltip says which rule changed it, and the game's value. Only modded weapons shows those vanilla WARNO doesn't have: your mod's copies, and those of a game mod chosen as the source.

Changing a Weapon

  • The Weapon pane shows every value of the weapon's ammunition, in sections: Damage, Range, Accuracy, Rate of Fire, Use, Projectile, Detection and Display. Hover over a value's name to see what it does in the game, its name in the file, and how sure that is.
  • A name marked ≈ is known from its name and how the game uses it, not from documentation. One marked ? is shown only: what it does is not known, so it can't be changed until it has been tried in the game.
  • Click a number to change it; the box says what it takes, such as the levels the weapon's kind of damage has. Switches turn a value on or off; a click on a choice lists the values the game's weapons have. A kind of damage is offered only when it has the weapon's level.
  • A value shown as – is one the weapon's ammunition doesn't have, and a rule can't add it, so it can't be changed. References to other descriptors (the missile, fire, smoke) are shown only.
  • A change reaches every unit that carries the weapon; the pane says how many before you change anything.
  • Switching on Must deploy warns first when units carrying the weapon have no other weapon that must deploy, which the game may not take, and names them. I Know What I'm Doing makes the change; nothing is refused.
  • To change a weapon for one unit only, right-click it in the unit's weapons and choose Copy for This Unit: the unit (and any unit sharing its loadout) gets a copy of its own, and the others keep the original.
  • Settings › Armory › Show names in the files shows, under each value's name in the Unit and Weapon panes, the property the game's files keep it in.
  • The ✎ on the picture gives the weapon another weapon's picture, from the game's own.
  • Shots per salvo is not changed here: weapons sharing an ammo box must fire the same number a salvo, which only a unit's loadout can check.
  • Changes are written by the Armory's Weapons rule set on the Mods tab, as locked rules. They need the weapon's file (Ammunition.ndf or AmmunitionMissiles.ndf) on the Files tab.

New Weapons

  • + New Weapon... makes a weapon of your own: pick the weapon it copies. An ammunition has some 60 values, many of them references, so a new weapon is never blank. It is carried by no unit until you give it to some, under Used By, or mount it with Swap in a unit's loadout.

A Copy for Some Units

  • To change a weapon for some units only, tick them under Used By (or click Copy...), name the copy and click Copy for N units. The copy is a new weapon in your mod: same picture, flash and sound, every value the same until you change it. The other units keep the original.
  • The copy needs WeaponDescriptor.ndf on the Files tab too: the ticked units' loadouts are pointed at it.
  • Units sharing a loadout carry the same weapons, so they are ticked together: a unit you add in the Armory shares its model unit's loadout.
  • A copy's own pane can give units the original back, and a weapon's pane can give units a copy you made before.
  • In the game, a copy shows under its original's name.

To take a change back, type the game's value again, use Undo, or delete its rules from the Weapons rule set.

pages.title: The Settings Tab
pages.html:
Options for exporting, the look of the app, and your saved data.

pages.title: Settings
pages.html:
Settings are in groups; the search box at the top finds one by name.

Export

SettingWhat it does

"Edited with EasyNDF" commentThe first line added to edited files, with the version.

Files and Results

File Editor

Line numbers, Word wrap, Scope linesNumbers down the side, long lines wrapping, and thin lines down each level of indentation.
Close brackets and quotesTyping ( [ { " or ' also types its partner.

Appearance

pages.title: Themes
pages.html:
• Pick a look under Theme in Settings. Automatic follows your computer's light or dark mode: Paper when it is light, Slate when it is dark.
  • New from this theme makes your own copy to change: colors and fonts, with a live preview.
  • Your own themes can be renamed, exported and shared.

Built-in Themes

Olivine (the default), Automatic, Slate, Paper, Dusk, Lilac, Ember, Blush, Cartridge, Basalt, Monokai, Mariana, Solarized Dark and Solarized Light.

Other Looks

  • Beveled edges gives buttons and boxes raised and sunken edges in any theme. Off makes any theme flat.
  • Fonts... chooses the interface font and the code font, for every theme. The code list shows fixed-width fonts, which keep NDF text lined up.
  • Tread scrollbars gives scrollbars a raised thumb with a grip, in a sunken track.
  • Interface size makes everything larger or smaller.
  • Reset column widths puts every table back to automatic widths.

More About Your Own Themes

  • Change any color with the picker or a code like #1c221e. You see the change straight away in the app and in the preview.
  • There are separate colors for errors and warnings, the toggle sliders, and the old and new lines of Changes only.
  • Themes can also be deleted, reset and imported. Built-in themes can't be changed.

pages.title: Backups and Clearing Data
pages.html:
• Everything you make is saved on this computer, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\EasyNDF. In portable mode, set by a file called EasyNDF portable mode.txt beside EasyNDF.exe, it's in a Data folder beside the app instead.
  • Back up all mods, in Settings, saves all your mods in one file. Restore backup... brings them back.
  • Reset settings puts the settings back but keeps your mods.
  • Clear all data deletes everything EasyNDF has saved.

More Details

  • These buttons are under Data in Settings.
  • Clear all data also empties the file list. The two built-in mods come back.
  • Export mod, on the Mods tab, saves one mod at a time.

pages.title: Handy Tricks
pages.html:
• Right-click almost anything for a menu of what you can do with it.
  • Ctrl+Z undoes changes on the Files and Mods tabs.
  • A text box with a small arrow at its end has more text than fits. Click the arrow to see it all.
  • Drag the bar between two parts of a tab, like the file list and Details, to share the room differently. Double-click the bar to reset it.
  • Drag a column heading to move the column, or the line between headings to resize it.

More Tricks

  • Right-click works on rows, headings, folders, rules, edits in Details, the Editor's text and lists, and most dropdowns. Text boxes have the usual Cut, Copy and Paste menu.
  • In the bigger text box, moving away or Enter keeps what you typed; Escape throws it away.
  • The ▥ and ▤ buttons on Details and Descriptors put them beside or below; click the pressed one again to let the window's size decide.
  • Every tab has a ? button at its top right with help for that tab.

pages.title: Limits
pages.html:
• EasyNDF makes sure an exported file can be read. It can't tell whether the game will like your values, so test your mod in the game.
  • Every GameData file of WARNO and Steel Division 2 can be read and exported. Conditions, comparisons and the like inside them are kept as written: rules change the plain values around them.
  • Very large files, like Steel Division 2's 117 MB UniteDescriptor.ndf, take several seconds and a lot of memory to read and run.
  • Undo doesn't cover Settings.
  • Rule sets that use anything but plain Edit rules won't work in the old EasyNDF desktop app.

More Limits

  • A file EasyNDF can't read says "Could not read or parse", and can still be exported as an unchanged copy.
  • A password-protected .zip or .rar can't be opened, and a .rar over 1.5 GB is refused. Extract them and add the folder instead.
  • Two files with the same name in different folders are told apart by folder. Each has its own property scan.
  • Adding, subtracting and multiplying whole numbers is exact at any length. Any other calculation on a number with more than 15 digits leaves it alone, with a warning. With Decimal places set to 0, numbers keep 12 significant digits.
  • The Editor has its own undo.

pages.title: About
pages.html:

More Details

  • The About tab also has who made the tool, credits and special thanks.
  • Change log lists what changed in each version, newest first. Clicking the version next to the title opens it too.
  • License opens the license: the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3, with two additional terms about the name.

pages.title: 1. Find the Mods Folder
pages.html:
These pages are about the game's own mod tools, not EasyNDF. The game's Mods\ReadMe.txt and modding manual have every detail.

In Steam, right-click WARNO, then Manage, then Browse local files. Open the Mods folder.

Steel Division 2 works the same way: its Mods folder has the same .bat files and a ModData\base.zip. Read WARNO as Steel Division 2 in these pages.

pages.title: 2. Make Your Mod
pages.html:
You only do this once per mod.

  1. In the Mods folder, click the address bar at the top, type cmd and press Enter. A black window opens.
  2. Type CreateNewMod.bat MyMod and press Enter. Use your own name. If it has spaces, put it in double quotes: CreateNewMod.bat "My Mod".

You now have a folder called WARNO\Mods\MyMod. Its GameData folder holds the game's files. Leave the other files in there as they are.

pages.title: 3. Get the Clean Files
pages.html:
The game keeps its untouched files zipped in WARNO\Mods\ModData\base.zip. Steam keeps it up to date with the game. These are the files to add in EasyNDF.

Getting Them

Unzip base.zip into a folder outside the game, like Documents\WARNO clean, and add the GameData folder inside it.

CarefulAlways add these files on the Files tab, not your mod's own GameData. Your mod gets your edited files, and running your rules on those again would apply them twice.

pages.title: 4. Put Your Changes In
pages.html:
Have Run export write straight into your mod:

  1. On the Files tab, press Select all.
  2. Press Export folder... and choose WARNO\Mods\MyMod. Choose the mod folder itself, not the GameData inside it.

From then on, Run export writes straight into your mod, replacing the files it wrote last time. Back up overwritten files in Settings keeps the old ones as .bak.

Or press Save as zip... after an export and unzip it into WARNO\Mods\MyMod.

pages.title: 5. Build It and Play
pages.html:
1. Double-click GenerateMod.bat in WARNO\Mods\MyMod and wait for it to finish. Do this after every export.
  2. Start WARNO, open the Mod Center, and turn your mod on.

pages.title: 6. Share It
pages.html:
• UploadMod.bat, in your mod's folder, puts it on the Steam Workshop.
  • Changed how the game plays? Raise the Version number in your mod's Config.ini before uploading, or players with different versions can't play together. It's in Saved Games\EugenSystems\WARNO\mod\MyMod.
  • Want your name in the files? See Watermark.

pages.title: 7. After a Game Update
pages.html:
After the game updates, GenerateMod.bat won't build your mod until the mod is updated too.

  1. Double-click UpdateMod.bat in your mod's folder. It brings your mod up to the new game version. If it lists files that need fixing by hand, files EasyNDF exports can be skipped: press Enter, and your next export replaces them.
  2. Get fresh clean files: unzip the new base.zip.
  3. Add them in EasyNDF, export into your mod, and run GenerateMod.bat.

Your rules work on the new files without any extra effort.

If a rule now changes nothing, the game probably renamed what it was looking for. Details tells you which rule.

quickHelp.title: Rules
quickHelp.html:
Conditions pick which descriptors change. A descriptor is one entry in the file, such as one kind of ammo.

Any: one condition is enough. All: every condition must match.

Actions change properties of those descriptors.

Property scan, at the bottom, fills the Operand and Target lists from a file.

quickHelp.title: Conditions
quickHelp.html:
Operand: what to look at, such as Descriptor Title (the descriptor's name) or a property.

Operator and Value: the test, such as Starts With Ammo_DCA.

(not in scan): no file has been scanned yet. Property scan, at the bottom of the rule, fills the list.

While you type, suggestions appear: Enter puts one in, Ctrl+Space opens them.

quickHelp.title: Actions
quickHelp.html:
Target: the property to change.

Operator and Value: the change, such as Multiply by 3.

Comment: a note written beside the change in the exported file.

While you type, suggestions appear: Enter puts one in, Ctrl+Space opens them.

quickHelp.title: Filter Descriptors
quickHelp.html:
Shows only the descriptors whose properties pass the conditions. The Property list holds the properties found in the descriptors being viewed.

The checkbox turns a condition on or off. Right-click a condition to move, copy or delete it.

A filter works without saving it. Save as... keeps it under a name; Export and Import... share saved filters as a file.

quickHelp.title: Watermark
quickHelp.html:
Writes Author, Mod version and Game version as a comment at the top of every file this mod exports.

Ask on export asks before each export. Off by default; saved in the mod file.
